quote_text:
A really hard-fought, much-needed win?
Hard-fought definitely, but that was not  a surprise. Nine games in a row, unbeaten.  
Everton hardly ever concede a goal, hardly  ever concede a chance. Defend with 10 players,  
apart from Beto, in and around their 18-yard  box. With players like Tarkowski and Branthwaite,  
it is almost of no use to bring a cross  in because they head every ball away.
So a team that is difficult to play against  because they're also a threat in the counterattack  
with Beto. And every throw-in they get, every  free-kick they get—and against us they get quite  
a lot of free-kicks, that was a joke... um, you  have to defend that. And from that sometimes—what,  
you didn't like that joke? Okay. Um,  and that's what makes it so difficult.
So what I liked much more today than I  liked at Goodison Park—Goodison Park we  
had ball possession, but we only had  ball possession with our centre-backs  
and our full-backs. And today, only  the first half, I think if I say 10,  
15 times that Dominik Szoboszlai was  one-v-one against Mykolenko, I don't even  
think I exaggerate. But to have that is one  thing. To create a chance is a second thing.
So that's why we had to be there  so many times, so many times,  
so many times. And you're hoping that one time  then can be enough. And it was, with Jota.
Very pleased. He was close to it already in  the first half. I think it was after seven,  
eight or nine minutes. But it was not  a surprise that they blocked that shot,  
because they—yeah—defensively,  incredible strong team. So yeah,  
for him to come up in the second half—he  had two of these moments as well. And the  
other moment was blocked. But now he found  just a bit of space and he scored the goal,  
which was nice for him, but nice for us. And with  "us" I mean his teammates, the staff and the fans.
Were you surprised also that he  wasn’t sent off for what followed?
Let me first say that I don’t want to  comment about the situation because so  
many people already commented on that, and even  people that are not liking Liverpool a lot.  
And they were all so clear and  obvious what the decision should  
have been that there's no need for me  to comment on that. Was I surprised? No.
Well… it's not something that came up last  week. It's something that I thought about—we  
thought about—for a bit longer. First half  of the season there were already moments  
where I talked about this with him. That  I think he's able to do this in games or  
in moments of games. But three full-backs were  injured—Trent Alexander-Arnold, Conor Bradley  
and Joe Gomez. So then it's a choice of playing  a centre-back over there. Jarell [Quansah] did  
quite okay in that position, to be fair,  and he would have helped us with set-pieces.
But I felt—we felt—that if we would have a chance  to win the game, we had to play better with the  
ball than we did in the away game. So it's a  risk to play a midfielder over there, maybe,  
but I knew that he could help with his creativity  in that position, because that's what you lack,  
of course, when Trent is not playing for you.  And he did very well defensively also. So,  
strong performance from him, like from  the whole team, and nice to have an extra  
option in that position because three  of them are injured in that position.
Is that something I'm surprised about?
I don't mind if they take 10 seconds or a  minute. If you are VAR and you think it's  
no red card—yeah—then you can also say it in  10 seconds. You don't have to wait for me to  
look at it a minute. So, yeah, it's a human  being that makes the decision. So the referee  
makes the decision, a human being makes the  decision over there. So, I don't mind if they take  
10 seconds or a minute or two minutes or three  minutes. They should take the right decision.
And if I hear all the comments, people  don't think they made the right decision,  
which they fortunately did with the offside  goal—which was not offside according to the rules.
Do I like the rule? No, I don't like the  rule. I think it's a rule that is not  
helping the team that wants to attack. Because  normally we always go to the halfway line,  
they kick the ball long, the striker is in an  offside position and my centre-backs feel like,  
“Oh, I have to head the ball,  head the ball away.” I always  
tell the linesman, “It was offside.” He  says, “No, no, he's not interfering.”
So I hate that rule, but the execution of the rule  was, for us today, well done in that situation.
Well done. Thank you. See you in a moment.
title: Arne Slot Post Match Press Conference | Liverpool 1-0 Everton
